repositories.description: Use SuSy to Spot AI-Generated images

paragraphs: SuSy is a Spatial-Based Synthetic Image Detection and Recognition Model, designed and trained to detect synthetic images and attribute them to a generative model (i.e., two StableDiffusion models, two Midjourney versions and DALL·E 3). The model takes image patches of size 224x224 as input, and outputs the probability of the image being authentic or having been created by each of the aforementioned generative models.

The model is based on a CNN architecture and is trained using a supervised learning approach. It's design is based on previous work, originally intended for video superresolution detection, adapted here for the tasks of synthetic image detection and recognition. The architecture consists of two modules: a feature extractor and a multi-layer perceptron (MLP), as it's quite light weight. SuSy has a total of 12.7M parameters, with the feature extractor accounting for 12.5M parameters and the MLP accounting for the remaining 197K.

The CNN feature extractor consists of five stages following a ResNet-18 scheme. The output of each of the blocks is used as input for various bottleneck modules that are arranged in a staircase pattern. The bottleneck modules consist of three 2D convolutional layers. Each level of bottlenecks takes input at a later stage than the previous level, and each bottleneck module takes input from the current stage and, except the first bottleneck of each level, from the previous bottleneck module.

paragraphs: A terminal-native workbench that takes a protein and a plain-language goal, triages what kind of campaign it can run, drives an iterative loop that proposes and ranks variants, and ends at a finished design you take to a cloud lab.

When a registered combinatorial DMS landscape exists for the protein (GB1), the loop returns real assayed fitness. When no measured landscape exists, it runs a predict-only loop that ranks variants by computable in silico proxies, clearly labeled predicted rather than measured.

Framing rule: proposal and modeling run in silico. Measured values are real prior measurements from a published deep mutational scan, standing in for a live bench round; predicted values are in silico estimates and are labeled as such. repositories.description: Detect and understand fields in a form page

paragraphs: Public server-side demo for nutrientdocs/form-field-vlm. The commercial VLM is loaded from the private nutrientdocs/form-field-vlm-private repository using the Space's HFTOKEN secret; weights are never included in this Space.

The demo runs on Hugging Face ZeroGPU using Transformers with xgrammar-constrained JSON decoding. vLLM is reserved for persistent-GPU production deployments because its CUDA engine must remain resident. Nine named example forms cover government, insurance, employment, medical, financial, aviation, and multilingual layouts. Selecting an example fills the image input; inference starts only when Detect fields is pressed. The benchmark examples derive from CommonForms, CC-BY-4.0.

The hybrid path uses FF-DETR / CommonForms by jbarrow, Apache-2.0. The configured detector artifact is a Transformers-format conversion of the upstream model. FF-DETR contributes object detection and box localization only. It does not provide labels, fine field types, values, or radio-group links; those outputs come from the Nutrient VLM.
